subject: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot
messages:
From: Samir Kaur <samir@vertexapps.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@vertexapps.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot

Hi Olga / Markus,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call this morning. Vertex Apps is planning a two-week pilot (Nov 16–Nov 30) for our live chat product using Redwood's new Realtime API (beta). The pilot traffic pattern will be spiky (short bursts at peak minutes) and we anticipate some cold-starts as we iterate prompts.

For the pilot to meet our product goals we need a temporary modification to the published latency SLA for preview/beta endpoints — specifically: relax the p99 latency requirement from 300ms to 800ms for the preview model in us-west-2 for the duration of the pilot window, with the understanding this is temporary and would be evaluated afterward. We are open to compensating with a limited QPS cap and accepting reduced throughput.

Can Redwood approve a short-term SLA carveout for the pilot? If needed we can sign a one-off amendment or accept a scoped disclaimer.

Attachments: pilot_run_metrics_q3.csv (sample traffic from our internal alpha)

—Samir Kaur
Head of Product, Vertex Apps
samir@vertexapps.com
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kaur <samir@vertexapps.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the sample metrics. I dug into the pilot constraints with the runtime team and we can likely accommodate a scoped exception, but we need to lock down mitigations and operational guardrails before approving.

Proposed guardrails:
- Scope: preview Realtime model only, region us-west-2, pilot window Nov 16–Nov 30 (we can extend by mutual agreement)
- Latency: temporary p99 target relaxed to 800ms; p95 to remain ≤400ms
- Throughput: hard QPS cap (customer-provided target) to avoid noisy-neighbor escalation
- Observability: we require a shared telemetry dashboard and 5-minute alerting to your ops and our SRE on p95/p99 regressions
- Fallback: auto-failover to a smaller, quantized model when queue depth exceeds safe thresholds (details TBC)

Markus — can you confirm if legal/finance require an amendment or can we handle this as an operational carveout with a signature below? Hannah / Dev — can you confirm technical feasibility and what we need to instrument on our side?

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Samir Kaur <samir@vertexapps.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot

Samir / Olga — thanks. From a contracts perspective I would prefer a short amendment (one page) that explicitly scopes the carveout (dates, region, model id) and the rollback criteria. We can treat it as a limited-term SLA modification rather than a permanent change. Finance suggests a small credit (1–2% of monthly invoice for the pilot period) in exchange for the added operational overhead.

Operationally we will not approve account-wide SLA changes; approval is limited to the described pilot conditions only. Legal — please prepare a one-page amendment that includes: start/end dates, model identifier, metrics waived, monitoring obligations, and termination clause.

Attaching a draft (sla_draft_rtf.pdf) with boilerplate language for your review.

-Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Samir Kaur <samir@vertexapps.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot

Quick tech note — we ran a replay of a 2-hour peak from your pilot CSV and here are proposed mitigations we can implement before Nov 16: 
- Autoscaling: aggressive scale-on-burst policy for preview pool in us-west-2 (adds warm GPU nodes within 60s on simulated load)
- Model fallback: implement weighted routing so requests over threshold fall back to the quantized embedder (15% quality degradation but preserves throughput)
- Cache warmup: pre-warm KV cache for your session prefixes using the first-hour traffic pattern (script included)

We will instrument a shared Grafana with the following panels: p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue depth, active replicas, and error rate. I attached the replay snapshot (pilot_run_metrics_q3.csv) used for these tests. Please confirm the hard QPS cap you want — I recommend 60 QPS average with 180 QPS short bursts.

—Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Kaur <samir@vertexapps.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 17:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA modification for Realtime API pilot

Thanks team — the guardrails look reasonable and the draft amendment covers what our legal team needs. We accept the proposed QPS cap (60 avg / 180 burst) and the credit in lieu of added overhead. Please send the one-page amendment for signature (DocuSign preferred).

We appreciate the fast turnaround — this will let us proceed with our November pilot and provide real-world telemetry for both teams.

—Samir
Head of Product, Vertex Apps
